newsitem.title: UK: Brazil fixtures cited on sugar freight market.
newsitem.headline: Brazil fixtures cited on sugar freight market.

text.p: Firmer business dominated activity on the sugar freight market as Brazil remained the most popular quoted origin but new orders were thin on the ground, shipbrokers said on Friday. Fiji Sugar Marketing was said to have fixed 19/20,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Fiji to London at a rate close to $27.75 and shipbrokers cited market talk of a Fiji to Port Kelang fixture for 15,000 tonnes. Both orders were for 15/25 October. Mauritius Sugar Syndicate fixed 14,250/14,500 tonnes of bulk sugar from Port Louis to London at a rate reported at 14.25 stg, the same as for the last similar fixture. Glencore was said to have filled its recent prompt inquiry for 14,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Santos to Casablanca with Tunisia, Black Sea and Baltic options but no further details were available. Shipbrokers said Jean Lion privately fixed 14,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Brazil to Tunisia/Syria for 10/15 October and Scanports was said to have fixed 22,000 tonnes from north Brazil to Casablanca for September/October dates. The only new order of the day came from Cargill, said to be open for 25,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Santos/Recife/Maceio to Morocco, Egyptian Mediterranean or Black Sea options for early October.
